topic: Natural Language Processing: Transformers, Attention, and Tokenization

questions.scenario: A healthtech enterprise deployed an emergency room clinical decision system using a pre-trained general-domain RoBERTa model (utilizing standard Byte-Pair Encoding / BPE). During operational stress-testing, clinical notes containing complex medical terms (e.g., 'piperacillin-tazobactam' or 'thrombocytopenia') frequently hit the 512-sequence length limit and caused severe inference latency spikes, despite the raw input text being under 180 words. Investigation reveals that medical jargon is being fragmented into dozens of single-character or two-character sub-tokens.
questions.question: What is the root cause of this performance trade-off, and what is the most effective architectural solution?
options: A) BPE suffers from domain-out-of-vocabulary (OOV) vocabulary mismatch, causing extreme token fragmentation that inflates sequence length $N$ and triggers quadratic $O(N^2)$ attention memory overhead; solved by retraining a domain-adapted tokenizer (e.g., BioBPE/WordPiece) on medical corpora.
B) The absolute positional embeddings in RoBERTa duplicate tokens when hyphens are present; solved by replacing absolute positional embeddings with Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE).
C) The Scaled Dot-Product Attention mechanism suffers from numerical instability on subword sequences; solved by raising the attention temperature during inference.

D) Byte-Pair Encoding is inherently incapable of handling hyphenated medical terms; solved by bypassing subword tokenization completely and using pure character-level Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs).
questions.correct_answer_text: A) BPE suffers from domain-out-of-vocabulary (OOV) vocabulary mismatch, causing extreme token fragmentation that inflates sequence length $N$ and triggers quadratic $O(N^2)$ attention memory overhead; solved by retraining a domain-adapted tokenizer (e.g., BioBPE/WordPiece) on medical corpora.
questions.explanation: BPE tokenizers trained on general web text lack highly specific domain terminology in their vocabulary. When encountered, rare/OOV words are split into fine-grained character or sub-character tokens. A 180-word clinical note can inflate to >512 tokens. Because Self-Attention complexity scales quadratically ($O(N^2)$ in time and memory with sequence length $N$), this sequence inflation drastically increases latency and causes sequence truncation. Retraining/adapting the tokenizer vocabulary on domain-specific text merges these frequent subwords back into single domain tokens, keeping $N$ short.

questions.scenario: A fintech compliance team is building an automated legal document auditing pipeline that must process 12,000-token SEC filing reports in real-time under tight GPU memory constraints (single NVIDIA T4 16GB GPU). When using a vanilla Transformer encoder with standard Multi-Head Self-Attention, the system regularly throws CUDA Out-Of-Memory (OOM) exceptions even with a batch size of 1.
questions.question: Which attention mechanism modification directly addresses this memory wall while preserving long-range global context across the document?
options: A) Switch to Multi-Query Attention (MQA) which reduces the feed-forward network parameter count while maintaining standard dense $O(N^2)$ attention matrices.
B) Implement Local Sliding Window Attention combined with selective Global Tokens (e.g., Longformer architecture), reducing space complexity from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N)$.
C) Increase the number of attention heads $H$ while decreasing the per-head hidden dimension $d_k$, eliminating the quadratic dependency on sequence length.
D) Replace Cross-Attention layers with static Word2Vec vector averaging across fixed 512-token chunks.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Implement Local Sliding Window Attention combined with selective Global Tokens (e.g., Longformer architecture), reducing space complexity from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N)$.
questions.explanation: Standard Self-Attention computes an $N \times N$ matrix for sequence length $N$. For $N = 12,000$, $N^2 = 144,000,000$ elements per head per layer, causing massive GPU memory footprint ($O(N^2)$). Sparse attention mechanisms like Longformer use local windowed attention ($O(N \times w)$) for local context and designated global tokens ($O(N)$) for overall document representations, dropping total space and computational complexity to $O(N)$, which comfortably fits within 16GB VRAM.

questions.scenario: An e-commerce platform is deploying a conversational customer support bot using an auto-regressive Transformer decoder (e.g., LLaMA-style architecture). Under real-time operational benchmarking, latency per generated token increases linearly as the generated answer length grows from token 1 to token 512, exceeding the strictly enforced 20ms per-token streaming SLA.
questions.question: What is the primary computational bottleneck during auto-regressive inference, and how is it mitigated without retraining the underlying model?
options: A) Redundant computation of Key and Value vectors for historical tokens at every generation step; mitigated by implementing a Key-Value (KV) Cache.
B) High computational overhead of greedy token search; mitigated by switching to Beam Search with a beam width of 10.
C) Gradient recalculation during the forward pass; mitigated by enabling PyTorch automatic mixed precision (AMP) without changing the attention flow.
D) Softmax bottleneck in the final language model (LM) head; mitigated by applying Dynamic Quantization exclusively to the input embedding matrix.
questions.correct_answer_text: A) Redundant computation of Key and Value vectors for historical tokens at every generation step; mitigated by implementing a Key-Value (KV) Cache.
questions.explanation: In auto-regressive decoding, generating step $t$ requires attention over all previous $t-1$ tokens. Without caching, the model redundantly projects Query, Key, and Value states for all preceding tokens at every single step, leading to $O(t)$ work per token and overall $O(N^2)$ redundant computations. Implementing a KV Cache stores the Key and Value representations of previous tokens in GPU memory, meaning at step $t$, only the single new token's $Q, K, V$ are projected, reducing generation cost per token to $O(1)$ matrix-vector operations (memory-bound).
